card: This pull request fixes a typo in the miniscript_smart fuzz target upper bound, replacing 0x7FFFFFF with std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max(). Due to the missing hex digit, generated timelocks never exceeded LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD, completely missing test coverage for time-based after() nodes and Miniscript height/time mixing rules. Replaying the existing qa-assets corpus with the fix immediately increases coverage by 12 libFuzzer edges into previously unreached mixing branches.
evidence: PR description: 'With the fix, replaying the existing qa-assets corpus hits the mixing branches that previously had 0 hits (libFuzzer edges go from 8829 to 8841), and a 5 minute run covers the remaining ones.'
problem: ConsumeNodeSmart restricted older() and after() timelock values to [1, 0x7FFFFFF] instead of [1, 0x7FFFFFFF]. Because after() values never reached LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD (500,000,000), miniscript_smart never generated time-based after() nodes or exercised Miniscript's height-versus-time mixing checks in ComputeType.

risk.why: The change is strictly contained within fuzz test harness input generation.

summary: Fixes the upper bound for timelock generation in the miniscript_smart fuzz target by replacing an off-by-a-digit hex literal with std::numeric_limits<int32_t>::max(). This enables the fuzzer to generate timelock values equal to or exceeding LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD.
